text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000104's 99215 billing is concentrated on low-complexity patients and runs above peer rates at every complexity level, a pattern consistent with upcoding, though the chart evidence is too thin to confirm it.","leaning":"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding","interpretation":"The claims data point toward upcoding rather than a sicker panel. The excess over the risk-adjusted expectation persists in every complexity stratum, roughly double the all-provider share even for patients with no chronic conditions. Most 99215s fall on 0-1 condition patients with routine diagnoses such as UTI, follow-up, abdominal pain or rash (e.g., C0056901, C0057250, C0058000), while the high-complexity 99215s (e.g., C0057200, C0057624) look appropriate. The documentation cannot settle the question: only 3 documented 99215s came back. One was unsupported (C0056935, moderate MDM). The two supported ones (C0057470, C0057654) are themselves 0-condition UTI and follow-up visits documented as high MDM, which is plausible but worth scrutiny for inflated or templated notes. The modest peer z-score and the few data-reviewed notes lacking a lab line are weak signals on their own. A reviewer should first request a larger targeted sample of charts for low-complexity 99215 claims, starting with the sampled claims above, and compare MDM elements and time against the visit's actual content."}
